subject: Mathematics
chapterName: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates

questions.topic: Page 3: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 3-4 Focus)
questions.questionText: A student claims that for any two points (a, b) and (b, a), the location on the Cartesian plane remains identical regardless of the values of a and b. Provide a mathematical counter-argument to disprove this claim, specifically addressing the relationship between coordinate order and axis distance.
questions.correctAnswer: The claim is false; (a, b) and (b, a) represent the same point only if a = b. Otherwise, they represent different distances from the x and y axes.
questions.explanationAnswer: The claim is incorrect because the Cartesian coordinate system is an ordered pair system. The first coordinate (x) measures distance from the y-axis, and the second coordinate (y) measures distance from the x-axis. If a is not equal to b, the point (a, b) will have a different horizontal and vertical displacement compared to (b, a), placing them at different locations in the plane.
questions.explanationQuestion: To disprove the claim, one must demonstrate that the order of coordinates is non-commutative. By defining the x and y components as distinct distances from the axes, it becomes clear that swapping them changes the geometric position unless the values are identical.

subjective_evaluation_points.point: Correctly identifying that Cartesian coordinates are ordered pairs.
Explaining that the first coordinate corresponds to the distance from the y-axis and the second to the x-axis.
Providing the condition a = b for points to be identical.
Concluding clearly that swapping coordinates changes the geometric position when a is not equal to b.
